weeks.title: Reconnaissance, Attack Surface Mapping & OSINT
weeks.objective: Master passive DNS enumeration, port scanning with Nmap, and finding exposed staging assets.

slides.title: Passive Reconnaissance & Subdomain Enumeration
slides.content: 90% of bug bounty success is reconnaissance. Organizations frequently leave forgotten staging servers, unauthenticated Jenkins build servers, and misconfigured S3 buckets exposed on forgotten subdomains. Tools like subfinder, amass, and assetfinder map the complete attack surface.
slides.keyTakeaway: You cannot defend or audit what you cannot see; discovery precedes exploitation.

slides.title: Nmap & Port Fingerprinting
slides.content: Port scanning identifies live listening services. Differentiating open, closed, and filtered ports across standard (80, 443, 22) and non-standard ports (8080, 8443, 9000) exposes vulnerable internal microservice dashboards.
slides.keyTakeaway: Service version banners reveal outdated software with published CVE exploits.

practicalLab.title: Lab 1: Attack Surface Recon on Simulated Dubai Target
practicalLab.brief: Execute passive reconnaissance against an authorized target, identifying hidden subdomains and open ports without generating active alerts.
practicalLab.deliverable: Strategic project deliverable verified against commercial metrics.
practicalLab.proTip: Document every architectural tradeoff and execution boundary.

caseStudy.scenario: A company thinks they only have 2 servers. Your recon uncovers an unauthenticated staging server on stage-api.target.ae with admin access. What is the root cause?

options.text: Shadow IT / forgotten test deployment left exposed to public DNS without firewall protection
options.explanation: Staging environments are often neglected by developers and lack production security controls.
Passive DNS enumeration is public and deterministic.

quiz.question: What is the difference between Active and Passive reconnaissance?
options: Active directly sends network packets to the target; Passive gathers public intelligence without touching target infrastructure
Active is illegal, passive is boring
quiz.explanation: Passive recon leaves zero log footprint on the target system.

quiz.question: What does Nmap do?
options: Scans networks for live hosts, open ports, and running service versions
quiz.explanation: Nmap is the industry standard for network discovery and vulnerability scanning.

quiz.question: What is Shodan?
options: A search engine for internet-connected devices, servers, webcams, and open industrial systems
quiz.explanation: Shodan crawls and indexes open ports and service banners globally.

quiz.question: What is an S3 Bucket Misconfiguration vulnerability?
options: A bucket of water falling on a computer
Cloud storage permissions set to 'Public Read/Write', exposing internal documents to the internet
quiz.explanation: Publicly accessible S3 buckets leak sensitive databases and customer documents.

quiz.question: What is OSINT in cybersecurity?
options: Open Source Intelligence gathered from publicly available records and social platforms
quiz.explanation: OSINT gathers actionable intelligence from publicly accessible sources.

weeks.title: OWASP Top 10: Injections, XSS & Broken Access Control
weeks.objective: Intercept traffic with Burp Suite, exploit Cross-Site Scripting, and execute parameterized SQL defenses.

slides.title: Burp Suite: The Web Security Intercept Proxy
slides.content: Burp Suite operates as a man-in-the-middle proxy between the browser and web servers. Testers inspect raw HTTP/S headers, tamper with parameters in Repeater, and fuzz endpoints in Intruder to detect hidden administrative parameters.
slides.codeSnippet:
POST /api/user/profile HTTP/1.1
Host: target.ae
Content-Type: application/json

{"username": "citizen", "role": "superadmin"}  <-- Parameter Tampering
slides.keyTakeaway: Never trust client-side validation; intercept raw requests to test server-side controls.

slides.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) & Content Security Policy (CSP)
slides.content: XSS occurs when an application includes untrusted user data in a web page without proper encoding, allowing attackers to execute JavaScript in the victim's session. Modern defenses require Content Security Policy (CSP) headers and context-aware HTML escaping.
slides.keyTakeaway: Stored XSS hijacks session cookies; sanitize inputs and enforce strict CSP headers.

practicalLab.title: Lab 2: Intercept & Tamper Raw Requests in Burp Suite
practicalLab.brief: Capture API traffic, bypass client-side form validation, and test 10 reflective input parameters for sanitization flaws.
practicalLab.deliverable: Strategic project deliverable verified against commercial metrics.
practicalLab.proTip: Document every architectural tradeoff and execution boundary.

caseStudy.scenario:
A search input field reflects user queries directly into the DOM: `

Results for: USER_INPUT

`. What payload verifies XSS?

options.explanation: Injecting an executable HTML/JS tag triggers the DOM execution parser if unescaped.

quiz.question: What is Burp Suite primarily used for?
options: Intercepting, inspecting, and modifying HTTP/S traffic between clients and web applications
quiz.explanation: Burp Suite is the industry-standard web penetration testing proxy.

quiz.question: What is XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)?
options: An injection vulnerability where malicious JavaScript executes inside the victim's browser session
quiz.explanation: XSS enables attackers to steal session cookies and impersonate users.

quiz.question: What does SQL Injection exploit?
options: Unsanitized user inputs concatenated directly into dynamic SQL query strings
quiz.explanation: SQL injection allows attackers to run arbitrary database queries via unescaped input.

quiz.question: How are SQL Injection vulnerabilities definitively prevented in modern applications?
options: By asking users to be honest
Using Parameterized Queries (Prepared Statements) or type-safe ORMs
quiz.explanation: Prepared statements treat user input as inert data parameters rather than executable SQL code.

quiz.question: What is CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery)?
options: An attack that tricks an authenticated user into executing unwanted actions on a trusted web application
quiz.explanation: CSRF exploits ambient session cookies to submit forged state-changing requests.

weeks.title: API Security, BOLA/IDOR & Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
weeks.objective: Exploit Broken Object Level Authorization, privilege escalation, and internal cloud metadata endpoints.

slides.title: BOLA/IDOR: The #1 API Vulnerability
slides.content: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA/IDOR) occurs when an API endpoint takes an object ID parameter (e.g. GET /api/documents/1042) without verifying if the authenticated user owns that specific document. Changing '1042' to '1043' immediately leaks another customer's confidential record.
slides.keyTakeaway: Always enforce tenant and ownership validation on every individual object lookup.

slides.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) & Cloud Metadata
slides.content: SSRF occurs when a web application accepts a URL from a user (e.g. 'Fetch profile picture from URL') and fetches it without restricting internal IP addresses. Attackers supply cloud metadata URLs (169.254.169.254) to extract temporary IAM credentials and take over the entire cloud infrastructure.
slides.keyTakeaway: Never allow servers to query internal private IP addresses (10.x.x.x, 127.0.0.1, 169.254.x.x).

practicalLab.title: Lab 3: Exploit and Patch an IDOR Vulnerability in a REST API
practicalLab.brief: Identify an authorization bypass in a simulated Dubai banking API, extract admin records, and write the backend patch.
practicalLab.deliverable: Strategic project deliverable verified against commercial metrics.
practicalLab.proTip: Document every architectural tradeoff and execution boundary.

caseStudy.scenario: An API endpoint `/api/v1/invoices?id=8841` returns the invoice for any ID entered without checking who is logged in. What vulnerability is this?

options.text: BOLA / IDOR (Broken Object Level Authorization / Insecure Direct Object Reference)
options.explanation: Failing to verify ownership of referenced IDs is the definition of BOLA/IDOR.
The query parameter is valid, but authorization checks are missing.

quiz.question: What is BOLA / IDOR in API security?
options: A vulnerability where changing an object ID parameter exposes another user's private data due to missing ownership checks
quiz.explanation: BOLA occurs when server endpoints fail to check if the requesting user owns the requested object.

quiz.question: What is Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)?
options: A flaw where an attacker tricks a backend server into making requests to internal or unintended resources
quiz.explanation: SSRF weaponizes server network trust to access private internal networks and cloud metadata.

quiz.question: What is the critical cloud metadata IP address targeted in AWS/GCP/Azure SSRF exploits?
quiz.explanation: 169.254.169.254 is the standard link-local address for cloud instance metadata and IAM credentials.

quiz.question: What is Privilege Escalation?
options: An attacker exploiting a vulnerability to gain higher permissions (e.g. standard citizen to root superadmin)
quiz.explanation: Privilege escalation allows unauthorized users to usurp administrative control.

quiz.question: What does JWT stand for in modern API authentication?
options: JSON Web Token — a cryptographically signed compact assertion of user identity and claims
quiz.explanation: JWTs provide signed tokens representing authenticated user sessions across stateless APIs.

weeks.title: Responsible Disclosure, Bug Bounty Programs & Capstone Penetration Test
weeks.objective: Learn HackerOne/Bugcrowd bounty triage, drafting professional reports, and ethical legal boundaries.

slides.title: Bug Bounty Economics & Responsible Disclosure
slides.content: Top ethical hackers earn hundreds of thousands of dollars discovering vulnerabilities on platforms like HackerOne, Bugcrowd, and Dubai Police eCrime bounties. Responsible disclosure mandates private reporting, clear reproduction steps, and giving organizations reasonable remediation time before public discussion.
slides.codeSnippet:
Report Structure:
1. Title & Severity (CVSS Score)
2. Vulnerability Description
3. Step-by-Step Reproduction Proof of Concept
4. Business Impact Analysis
5. Recommended Remediation Code
slides.keyTakeaway: Clear, reproducible reports get validated faster and receive top-tier bounty payouts.

slides.title: UAE Cyber Law & Ethical Boundaries
slides.content: Under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 34 of 2021 concerning Combatting Rumors and Cybercrime, unauthorized penetration testing without explicit written consent is illegal. Ethical whitehats operate strictly within declared program scopes (Rules of Engagement).
slides.codeSnippet: Golden Rule: If a target is not listed in an authorized bounty scope, do not touch it.
slides.keyTakeaway: Adherence to scope separates elite whitehat researchers from criminal actors.

practicalLab.title: Lab 4: Capstone — Complete an End-to-End Penetration Test & Report
practicalLab.brief: Execute a full security assessment of a staged enterprise environment, document 3 vulnerabilities, and write a formal C-suite audit report.
practicalLab.deliverable: Strategic project deliverable verified against commercial metrics.
practicalLab.proTip: Document every architectural tradeoff and execution boundary.

caseStudy.scenario: You discover an SQL injection flaw in a major Dubai financial institution's public portal that is NOT in a bug bounty program. What do you do?

options.text: Report it responsibly directly to the Dubai Police eCrime department or the organization's certified security contact, without public disclosure
options.explanation: Responsible private disclosure protects public data and complies with UAE cyber laws.

options.text: Post the exploit code on Twitter immediately
options.explanation: Public disclosure before patching endangers users and violates UAE cybercrime statutes.

options.text: Dump the database and demand a ransom
options.explanation: Extortion is a severe criminal offense.

quiz.question: What is the primary difference between a Whitehat and Blackhat hacker?
options: Whitehats operate with explicit legal authorization to find and fix bugs; Blackhats violate laws for illicit gain
quiz.explanation: Authorization and ethical intent define whitehat security research.

quiz.question: What is CVSS in vulnerability assessment?
options: Common Vulnerability Scoring System, standardizing the severity rating of security flaws (0.0 to 10.0)
quiz.explanation: CVSS provides an objective numerical score quantifying the severity of security vulnerabilities.

quiz.question: What is a Proof of Concept (PoC) in bug reporting?
options: A minimal reproducible demonstration proving that a security flaw exists and can be triggered
quiz.explanation: PoCs demonstrate verifiable vulnerability impact to security triage teams.

quiz.question: What does Dubai's UAE Cyber Security Council oversee?
options: National cyber resilience, threat intelligence sharing, and safeguarding critical national digital infrastructure
quiz.explanation: The Cyber Security Council leads federal defense, cyber drills, and critical infrastructure hardening.

quiz.question: Why must penetration testers never test targets outside the declared 'Scope of Engagement'?
options: It is illegal under cybercrime laws to test systems without written authorization
quiz.explanation: Testing unauthorized systems constitutes illegal computer intrusion regardless of intent.

questions.question: What is BOLA / IDOR in API security?
options: Missing authorization checks when referencing objects by ID, allowing unauthorized data access
questions.explanation: BOLA occurs when endpoints return data by ID without verifying user ownership.

questions.question: What does Burp Suite proxy allow security researchers to do?
options: Intercept, inspect, and modify HTTP/S requests between client and server
questions.explanation: Burp Suite intercepts raw web traffic for security analysis.

questions.question: How are SQL Injection vulnerabilities definitively prevented?
questions.explanation: Prepared statements treat user input as inert data rather than executable SQL code.

questions.question: What does SSRF exploit?
options: A backend server making unintended requests to internal network services or cloud metadata
questions.explanation: SSRF tricks servers into querying private internal endpoints.

questions.question: What is the standard link-local IP address for cloud instance metadata in SSRF exploits?
questions.explanation: 169.254.169.254 provides instance metadata across AWS, GCP, and Azure.

questions.question: What is XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)?
options: Executing malicious JavaScript inside the victim's authenticated browser session
questions.explanation: XSS executes arbitrary scripts in user sessions to steal cookies and tokens.

questions.question: What does Content Security Policy (CSP) do?
options: Restricts the sources from which scripts, styles, and assets can be loaded to mitigate XSS
questions.explanation: CSP restricts unauthorized script execution by whitelisting trusted script origins.

questions.question: What is the role of the UAE Cyber Security Council?
options: Leading national cyber defense, threat intelligence, and critical infrastructure hardening
questions.explanation: The Cyber Security Council safeguards critical national digital infrastructure.

questions.question: What is CVSS?
options: Common Vulnerability Scoring System (0.0 to 10.0 scale evaluating severity)

questions.question: Why is testing targets outside declared bug bounty scope illegal?
options: Unauthorized access to computer systems violates federal cybercrime legislation
questions.explanation: Testing without explicit authorization violates computer trespass statutes.
